title: FloodGuard Rate Manual: Additional Premium for a Midterm Limit Increase
content:
### Section — Premium for a midterm limit increase (FloodGuard Private Flood Policy)

**(a) Charge.** The additional premium charged for a limit increase is the annual premium change recorded on the limit increase entry multiplied by the earned share of the increase, rounded half-up to the cent once at the end; when that figure is below the tier's minimum premium change, nothing is charged.

**(b) Earned share.** The earned share of the increase is the calendar days from the date the increase attaches to the expiration date divided by the calendar days in the term.

**(c) Entry read.** The limit-increase entry read is the most recently requested building limit increase on the policy. It supplies the annual premium change (the full-year premium of the increase), the date the increase attaches and the date it was requested. The expiration date and the start of the term are those on the policy.

**(d) Assembly.** The earned share and every share, load, credit and discount rated on the increase each multiply the annual premium change in turn, each acting on the figure the one before produced. No intermediate figure is rounded; rounding half-up to the cent is applied only to the final charge, and that rounded figure is the one compared with the tier's minimum premium change.

**(e) Minimum.** A final figure at or above the tier's minimum premium change is charged in full; a final figure below it is not charged at all.

### Worked figures (hypothetical inputs)

The inputs below are chosen for illustration; they are not premiums or dates of any actual policy, and the tier minimum used is assumed to be 5.00.

1. A term runs from 2025-01-01 to 2026-01-01, 365 calendar days. A limit increase attaches on 2025-03-01 with an annual premium change of 300.00. From the attach date to the expiration date there are 306 calendar days. The charge is 300.00 multiplied by 306 and divided by 365, which is 251.5068…, rounded half-up to 251.51. It is above the minimum and is charged.
2. Same term; an increase attaches on 2025-10-01 with an annual premium change of 8.00. There are 92 calendar days to expiration; 8.00 multiplied by 92 and divided by 365 is 2.0164…, rounded to 2.02. That is below the assumed minimum of 5.00, so nothing is charged.
3. Same term; an increase attaches on 2025-07-01 with an annual premium change of 20.00. There are 184 calendar days to expiration; 20.00 multiplied by 184 and divided by 365 is 10.0821…, rounded to 10.08, which is charged.
